Sensitivities: random-intercept MixedLM per rearing brood gives -0.081 g (SE 0.016); restricted to manipulated broods only, -0.107 g (SE 0.018); tarsus outcome -0.032 mm per sibling (cluster-robust SE 0.008). All agree in sign and significance: each extra sibling reduces day-14 mass by roughly 0.08-0.11 g (about 1% of the 10.3 g mean). Test statistic: t (cluster-robust), value -6.436, df 3,662.
rows.predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size: the number of siblings a chick was actually reared with (day-14 rearing-brood size, signed as measured); larger values = more siblings = more sibling competition

rows.note: Linear mixed model (REML) of day-14 nestling mass (g) on net rearing brood-size manipulation, fitted to chicks from experimentally manipulated rearing broods only (rear_nest_trt 5 = enlarged, net manipulation +1 to +4; trt 6 = reduced, −1 to −4). Focal predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (signed number of chicks net added to the rearing brood; larger = more siblings = more competition, so larger values correspond to MORE of the declared estimand). Test statistic: z = −11.55 (normal approximation; inferential df = ∞ for the mixed-model z, with 2,716 chick observations and 319 clusters). Focal estimate: −0.1796 g (SE 0.0156) per sibling added — enlarging a brood by one chick reduces day-14 mass by ~0.18 g (~1.8% of mean mass). Outcome was complete in the supplied file; no rows dropped for missingness among focal variables. The sign is negative: sibling competition substantially reduces nestling growth.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (signed net chicks added to the rearing brood, −4 to +4; focal effect on day-14 mass)

rows.note: Focal model: linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, ML) of day-14 chick mass (g) on the signed net rearing manipulation, fitted to all chicks with complete data (n=3,594 chicks from 434 rearing broods; unmanipulated broods included with net manipulation=0). Fixed effects: net_rearing_manipulation (focal, signed net chicks added to the rearing brood via cross-fostering: positive=enlarged, negative=reduced, 0=unmanipulated), rear_nest_OH (rearing-nest hatch date), rear_nest_CS (rearing-nest original clutch size). Exclusions: rows with missing values in outcome or model variables ('.' coded as missing; 126 chicks dropped, mostly missing rear_nest_LD-adjacent fields/nest identifiers). Chick sex omitted because missing for 1,094 chicks. Sensitivity: restricting to manipulated broods only (n=2,709 chicks, 318 broods) gives -0.181 g (SE 0.015, z=-11.76), so the effect is robust to inclusion/exclusion of unmanipulated broods. Interpretation: each extra sibling added to a rearing brood reduces day-14 nestling mass by ~0.18 g, evidence that sibling competition reduces nestling growth. Observation unit: individual chick at day 14; design: cross-fostered brood-size manipulation (enlarged/reduced/unmanipulated), chicks clustered in rearing broods. Test statistic: z = -11.545.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (signed number of chicks added to the rearing brood by the cross-fostering manipulation; positive = enlarged, negative = reduced, 0 = unmanipulated)

rows.note: Linear mixed model (REML, statsmodels MixedLM) of day-14 chick mass (g) on the experimentally assigned proportional brood-size manipulation. Focal predictor = net_rearing_manipulation / rear_nest_CS: the signed fraction of the rearing nest's original clutch added (enlarged broods, trt 5) or removed (reduced broods, trt 6); e.g. +0.25 = brood enlarged by a quarter of its clutch = MORE sibling competition. Sample: manipulated broods only (unmanipulated nests excluded because they were not matched to manipulated pairs in clutch size or laying date); n = 2,698 chicks from 317 rearing nests, after dropping rows with missing lay date. Covariates: original clutch size (rear_nest_CS), lay date (rear_nest_LD), year fixed effects (2001-2003); random intercept for rearing nest (chicks clustered within broods; between-nest variance 0.60 g^2, residual 0.58 g^2). Outcome complete for all rows. Estimate = -1.902 g per unit proportional manipulation (z = -11.91, p < 0.001; model-based SE reported by MixedLM, z-reference inferential distribution, no finite df). Equivalently, enlarging a brood by 25% of its clutch size reduces day-14 mass by 0.475 g (SE 0.040). Larger values of the focal predictor mean MORE sibling competition, so orientation is as_declared and the negative sign indicates competition reduces nestling growth. Observation unit: individual chick; design: matched-pair brood-size manipulation experiment (2001-2003, Wytham Wood), effect estimated from between-nest assigned variation in competition.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation / rear_nest_CS (signed proportional brood-size manipulation: fraction of the original clutch added (+, enlarged) or removed (-, reduced); larger = more siblings = more competition)

rows.note: Linear mixed model (REML) of day-14 tarsus length (mm) fitted to 2,801 chicks from 332 experimentally manipulated rearing broods (Wytham Wood blue tits, 2001–2003). Focal predictor: signed experimental-treatment contrast trt_contrast = +1 for enlarged rearing broods (trt 5), −1 for reduced (trt 6), decoded via net_rearing_manipulation. Adjusted for rearing-nest hatching date (rear_nest_OH) and year fixed effects; random intercept for rearing nest (chicks clustered within broods, mean 8.4 per brood). Unmanipulated broods excluded (not matched to manipulated pairs in clutch size or laying date). No outcome or covariate rows excluded beyond missing rear_nest_OH. Estimate −0.1904 mm is half the enlarged-minus-reduced difference (enlarged ≈ 0.38 mm shorter tarsus); SE 0.0225, z = −8.470, p ≈ 2.4e-17, model-based inference (normal/z, no small-sample df correction; between-brood var 0.124, residual var 0.314). Observation unit: chick; design: brood-size manipulation experiment with cross-fostering, matched enlarged/reduced pairs. Larger values of the contrast (+1 = enlarged) mean MORE siblings/competition, so orientation is as_declared and the negative sign indicates competition reduces growth. Robustness: consistent negative effects under per-sibling scales (tarsus −0.066 mm/net chick, z = −8.93; mass −0.180 g/net chick) and realized brood size (tarsus −0.034 mm/chick).
rows.predictor: Signed experimental-treatment contrast: enlarged rearing brood (+1) vs reduced rearing brood (−1); coefficient is half the enlarged-minus-reduced difference in day-14 tarsus length (mm)

rows.note: Focal model: linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, ML) of day-14 chick mass (g) on realized sibling competition, fitted to 2,611 chicks with known molecular sex and complete covariates, from 325 rearing broods (observation unit = individual chick; chicks clustered within rearing nests via a random intercept). Focal predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size (number of siblings/competitors in the rearing nest at day 14), entered as a continuous signed covariate; each unit = one additional sibling competitor. Adjusted for chick sex (males 0.50 g lighter), original rearing-nest clutch size (coefficient ~0, indicating the brood-size effect is not parental-quality confounding), rearing-nest hatch date, and year fixed effects (2001-2003). Sensitivity analyses: same model without sex adjustment over all 3,668 chicks in 446 broods gives -0.0812 g/sibling (SE 0.016, z = -5.04); restricted to experimentally manipulated broods gives -0.107 g/sibling (SE 0.018); tarsus-length outcome (OLS, cluster-robust SE) gives -0.032 mm/sibling (SE 0.008, t = -3.92). All specifications agree in sign and magnitude. Test statistic: z (mixed-model Wald) = -6.024; inferential df: 2604 residual; fitted n = 2,611 chicks, 325 clusters.
rows.predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size: number of nestmates (sibling competitors) in the chick's rearing brood at day 14, entered as a continuous signed covariate (grams of day-14 mass per one additional sibling)

rows.note: Linear mixed model (REML, statsmodels MixedLM) of a nestling body-size outcome on the experimentally assigned sibling-competition contrast. Outcome: PC1 of standardized day-14 mass and tarsus length (equal loadings ±0.707, sign-oriented so higher = larger body; 80% of joint variance; units = SD of the index). Focal predictor: rear_nest net_rearing_manipulation (signed net chicks added at cross-fostering: enlarged +1..+4, reduced -1..-4), so one unit = one additional sibling/competitor; larger values = MORE competition (orientation as_declared), and the estimate is negative, meaning more siblings reduce growth. Sample: chicks in manipulated broods only (trt 5 enlarged, trt 6 reduced; unmanipulated broods excluded because they were not matched on clutch size or laying date), n=2,716 chicks from 319 rearing broods (observation unit = chick; clustering by rearing nest handled with a rearing-nest random intercept). Covariates: rearing-nest hatch date (rear_nest_OH) and year fixed effects (2001-2003); clutch size and lay date were not used (excluded by design policy); chick sex excluded (29% missing). Estimate -0.1728 SD per additional sibling, SE 0.0148, z = -11.65, p = 2.4e-31. Between-brood variance 0.52, residual 0.83. Corresponding mass-scale check (excluded as focal by policy but consistent): -0.180 g per sibling (SE 0.016). Design: brood-size manipulation experiment with matched cross-fostered pairs, 2001-2003, Wytham Wood blue tits. Inference uses model-based (REML) standard errors with z reference distribution (no finite df; z=11.6 far exceeds any conventional critical value).
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (signed net chicks added to the rearing nest at cross-fostering; enlarged = positive, reduced = negative)

rows.note: Linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, ML) of day-14 nestling mass (grams) on realized sibling competition: day_14_weight ~ d14_rear_nest_brood_size (linear, number of chicks alive in the rearing brood at day 14 = number of competitors) + rear_nest_LD (rearing-nest lay date, days) + year fixed effects (2001/2002/2003), with a random intercept for rearing nest (rear_nest_breed_ID). Sample: ALL rearing broods (enlarged, reduced, and unmanipulated) — n = 3,668 chicks from 446 broods; 52 of 3,720 chicks excluded for missing rearing-nest lay date; no chicks excluded for missing mass/tarsus (complete in file). '.'-coded columns coerced to missing/numeric. Chick sex excluded as covariate (missing for 1,094/3,720 chicks). Focal test: z = -5.905, p < 0.0001 (Wald z, large-sample; inferential df for residual = 3,663). Nest random-intercept variance 0.795 g^2, residual variance 0.539 g^2. Observation unit: individual chick; design: clustered (chicks within rearing broods), observational-experimental blend — brood sizes were partly experimentally manipulated via cross-fostering (enlarged/reduced) but the predictor used is realized brood size, which mixes assignment with nest-quality-driven variation (hence slightly attenuated vs. the manipulated-only estimate of -0.111 g/sibling). Sensitivity: focal effect with net_rearing_manipulation among manipulated broods was -0.18 g/sibling, direction and significance unchanged across all specifications.
rows.predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size — linear, signed per-additional-sibling effect of the number of chicks in the rearing brood at day 14 (realized sibling-competition exposure)

rows.note: Native scale: grams of day-14 nestling mass per additional sibling. Design: nest-level OLS on mean day-14 mass per rearing brood, so each nest is one independent observation (no clustering remains; chick-level LMM with nest random intercept gave the nearly identical -0.181, SE 0.015, as a robustness check). Sample: 318 experimentally manipulated rearing broods (trt 5 enlarged: net +1 to +4; trt 6 reduced: net -1 to -4); unmanipulated broods (trt 7) excluded because they were not matched to manipulated broods on clutch size or laying date. Outcome: mean day_14_weight (g) of chicks measured at day 14 in each brood (2,709 chicks underlie the 318 broods; 14 manipulated broods dropped for missing rear_nest_OH/rear_nest_CS). Covariates: rear_nest_OH (rearing-nest hatching date, days) and rear_nest_CS (original clutch size, eggs). Inference: t = -12.00, df = 314, p ≈ 3.6e-33, heteroscedasticity-robust (HC3) SE (classical SE 0.0156, essentially identical). Model: mean_mass ~ net_rearing_manipulation + rear_nest_OH + rear_nest_CS; R2 = 0.315. Interpretation: each additional sibling experimentally added to a brood reduces mean day-14 nestling mass by ~0.183 g (sd of chick mass is 1.19 g), strong evidence that sibling competition reduces nestling growth. Observation unit of analysis: rearing nest (fitted n = 318).
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation: signed net number of chicks added to (positive) or removed from (negative) the rearing brood via experimental cross-fostering; each +1 unit = one additional sibling competitor

rows.note: Focal analysis: brood-level OLS (aggregation to the rearing brood to handle within-nest dependence among chicks, avoiding mixed/cluster-robust methods). One row per rearing brood (n=446 broods, aggregating 3,668 chicks with complete covariates across all treatment categories: enlarged trt 5, reduced trt 6, unmanipulated trt 7). Outcome: mean day-14 mass (g) of chicks in the rearing brood. Focal predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size — realized number of nestlings in the rearing brood at day 14, i.e., the number of sibling competitors each chick faced, entered as a signed continuous variable (larger = more competitors = more competition, so orientation is as_declared; negative coefficient means competition reduces growth). Sensitivities: chick-level linear mixed model with rearing-nest random intercept gives -0.081 g (SE 0.016, t=-5.04); restricted to experimentally manipulated broods only, -0.103 g (SE 0.018); tarsus length outcome gives -0.032 mm per extra sibling (cluster-robust SE 0.008, t=-3.9). Clutch size is non-significant in all fits, supporting the competition interpretation over parental quality. Missing values (coded '.') coerced to NaN; sex covariate omitted due to 29% missingness. Conclusion: each additional sibling competitor reduces day-14 nestling mass by ~0.08 g (mean mass 10.3 g, so ~0.8% per sibling), a strong negative effect of sibling competition on nestling growth.
rows.predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size (day-14 rearing-brood size: realized number of sibling competitors per chick, continuous, signed as measured; larger = more sibling competition)

rows.note: Linear mixed model (REML, statsmodels MixedLM) of day-14 tarsus length (mm) on experimental brood-enlargement status, restricted to the 452-brood dataset's 332 manipulated rearing broods (trt 5 = enlarged, trt 6 = reduced; trt 7 unmanipulated excluded because unmanipulated broods were not matched on clutch size/lay date). Focal predictor: 0/1 dummy 'enlarged' (1 = experimentally enlarged rearing brood, 0 = reduced), i.e. the signed group difference in tarsus, enlarged minus reduced. Covariates: rearing-nest hatching date (rear_nest_OH) and year fixed effects (2001-2003); random intercept for rearing nest. Exclusions: only rows missing tarsus, treatment, hatch date, or nest ID (2801 of 3368 manipulated-brood chicks analyzed, 332 broods; chick-level sex excluded as a covariate because 1094/3720 chicks have unknown molecular sex). Estimate: -0.3809 mm (SE 0.0450), z = -8.470, p = 2.4e-17; nest-level variance 0.124, residual 0.314. Inference is z-based (no finite df; mixed-model z approximation). Observation unit: individual chick; clustering by rearing nest. Larger values of the dummy (enlarged broods) correspond to MORE sibling competition, so the orientation is as_declared; the negative sign indicates competition reduces nestling growth, consistent with sensitivity analyses (mass per net sibling added -0.18 g; tarsus per net sibling -0.066 mm; tarsus per realized day-14 brood-mate -0.034 mm).

rows.note: Model: linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, REML), day_14_tarsus_length (mm) ~ trt_score + rear_nest_OH + C(hatch_year), with a random intercept for rearing nest (rear_nest_breed_ID). Sample: all 3,720 chicks measured at day 14 in all 452 rearing broods (1,742 chicks in enlarged broods, 1,059 reduced, 919 unmanipulated); complete outcomes (tarsus, rear_nest_OH, treatment) required no exclusions. Focal predictor: signed treatment score trt_score = +1 enlarged (rear_nest_trt=5), 0 unmanipulated (trt=7), -1 reduced (trt=6); its coefficient is the enlarged-vs-reduced difference anchored by unmanipulated broods, in native tarsus-mm scale. Covariates: rearing-nest hatching date (rear_nest_OH) and year fixed effects (2001 reference); sex excluded (missing for 1,094 chicks). Result: estimate = -0.1921 mm per treatment-score unit (SE 0.0232, z = -8.296, p = 1.1e-16), i.e. chicks in enlarged broods have day-14 tarsus ~0.38 mm shorter than chicks in reduced broods — sibling competition reduces nestling growth. Inferential statistic: z (large-sample normal, MixedLM); no finite df (asymptotic). Observation unit: individual chick; chicks clustered in rearing nests (mean 8.2 chicks/brood) handled via nest random intercept (between-nest var 0.137, residual var 0.297). Note: unmanipulated broods were not matched on clutch size/laying date; the estimate including them (-0.192) matches the manipulated-broods-only contrast (-0.190, SE 0.023), indicating robustness. Other operationalizations all negative: -0.18 g mass per net sibling added; -0.066 mm tarsus per net sibling added; -0.034 mm per day-14 brood-mate.

rows.note: Focal model: nest-level OLS of brood-mean day-14 mass (g) on realized rearing-brood size at day 14. To satisfy dependence constraints (no random intercepts, no cluster-robust SEs), the data were aggregated to one row per rearing brood (n=447 broods, from 3,668 chicks with complete mass, brood-size, clutch-size, lay-date and year data), eliminating within-brood dependence by construction. Focal predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size (number of siblings/competitors a chick actually grew up with, continuous 1-17), larger values = MORE sibling competition (orientation as_declared). Covariates: original clutch size (rear_nest_CS), lay date (rear_nest_LD), breeding season (2001-2003 fixed effects). Estimate (native scale): -0.0769 g day-14 mass per additional sibling, SE 0.0162, t = -4.754, df = 441, p = 2.7e-06. Sensitivities all consistent: chick-level mixed model with brood random intercept gave -0.081 g (SE 0.016); chick-level cluster-robust OLS gave -0.097 g (SE 0.015); tarsus-length outcome gave -0.032 mm/sibling (cluster-robust SE 0.008); chick-weighted brood regression identical (-0.0769, SE 0.0162). Conclusion: each additional sibling reduces nestling day-14 mass by ~0.08 g (about 0.8% of the 10.3 g mean), strong evidence that sibling competition limits nestling growth.
rows.predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size (day-14 rearing-brood size, in number of chicks: realized sibling-competition exposure)

rows.note: Linear mixed model (REML) of day-14 nestling mass (g). Outcome: day_14_weight. Focal predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (signed net number of chicks added at the cross-fostering manipulation; positive = enlarged brood, negative = reduced; 0 for unmanipulated). Adjustment: an indicator for unmanipulated broods (because controls were not matched to manipulated pairs and differ in mean mass), rearing-nest hatching date (rear_nest_OH), and year fixed effects (2001-2003). Sample: all chicks alive and measured at day 14 with complete focal variables = 3,635 chicks from 439 rearing broods (85 dropped for missing rear_nest_OH; no missing mass or manipulation values). Chick sex was excluded as a covariate because it is missing for 1,094 chicks. Signed quantity: grams of day-14 mass per additional sibling (larger values of the predictor = more siblings = more competition, so orientation as_declared; expected effect negative). Estimate = -0.1802 g/sibling, SE = 0.0153, t(z) = -11.790, p = 4.4e-32; between-nest variance 0.595, residual variance 0.532. Observation unit = individual chick; design = chick-level outcomes clustered in rearing nests, with the sibling-competition exposure varying at the nest level. Sensitivity: restricting to manipulated broods only (n=2,716 chicks, 319 nests) gives essentially the same estimate (-0.180 g, SE 0.016).
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (signed net chicks added to the rearing brood at manipulation; g of day-14 mass per additional sibling)

rows.note: Focal analysis: Gaussian GEE with exchangeable working correlation within rearing brood and robust (sandwich) standard errors, fitted to day-14 nestling mass (g). Focal predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size — the realized number of sibling competitors a chick was reared with at day 14 (signed continuous count, nest-level, ranging 1–17). Covariates: rearing-nest original clutch size, rearing-nest lay date, and year fixed effects (2001–2003). Population: all 3,668 chicks (of 3,720) with complete focal outcome and covariates across manipulated and unmanipulated rearing broods; 446 rearing broods (mean 8.2 chicks each, exchangeable within-brood correlation estimated at rho ≈ 0.59). Exclusions: rows missing lay date or clutch size (52 chicks); chick sex excluded as covariate because 1,094 chicks lack molecular sex. Focal estimate (native scale, grams per additional sibling): −0.0813 g, robust SE 0.0151, z = −5.36, p ≈ 8.1e-08, 95% CI [−0.111, −0.052] on a mean mass of 10.3 g — each additional sibling reduces day-14 mass by ~0.08 g. GEE uses z-based inference; cluster count is 446 broods. Observation unit: individual chick. Corroborating analyses: linear mixed model with rearing-brood random intercept gives −0.0812 g (SE 0.0161, t −5.04, resid df 3,662) on the same data; restricted to experimentally manipulated broods only the slope is steeper (−0.107 g, SE 0.018); the skeletal outcome day-14 tarsus length shows the same pattern (−0.032 mm per sibling, cluster-robust SE 0.008, t −3.9). Clutch-size coefficient is near zero (−0.025, p 0.32), indicating the effect tracks competitor number rather than parental quality. Direction: larger brood size = more competition = lower growth.
rows.predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size (realized day-14 rearing brood size: number of sibling competitors, signed continuous count, one g of day-14 mass change per additional sibling)

rows.note: Linear mixed model (REML, statsmodels MixedLM) of day-14 nestling mass (g) on the number of siblings at the start of rearing. Data: 3,720 blue tit chicks (Wytham Wood, 2001–2003 brood-size manipulation/cross-fostering experiment). Focal predictor: rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing = brood size of the rearing nest immediately after the experimental manipulation (the number of competitors each chick faced from day 0; range 2–18, mean 10.6). Covariates: rearing-nest hatching date (rear_nest_OH) and year fixed effects (hatch_year 2001/2002/2003). Random intercept for rearing nest (rear_nest_breed_ID). Complete cases only: 3,333 chicks in 399 rearing broods (dropped due to missing rear_nest_OH). Chick sex was excluded as a covariate because it is missing for 1,094 chicks. Estimate: −0.1528 g per additional sibling (SE 0.0124, t = −12.30, p = 8.7e-35; z-based inference, no finite df — REML mixed model). Group (nest) variance 0.595, residual variance 0.539. Observation unit: individual chick at day 14; design: observational gradient in realized rearing brood size that includes the experimental brood-size manipulation (enlarged trt 5, reduced trt 6, unmanipulated trt 7 nests all included), with chicks clustered within rearing nests handled via random intercepts. Robustness: an alternative contrast (signed net_rearing_manipulation among manipulated broods only, adjusted for hatch date and year) gave a consistent estimate of −0.180 g per sibling (SE 0.016), indicating the conclusion is not construction-dependent. Orientation: larger brood size = more siblings = more sibling competition, and the effect is negative, i.e., more competition reduces growth.
rows.predictor: Rearing-nest brood size at the start of rearing (rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing, chicks per brood after the manipulation), as a continuous per-sibling linear contrast on day-14 mass

rows.note: Linear mixed model (REML, statsmodels MixedLM) of day-14 nestling mass (g) on the experimentally assigned proportional brood-size manipulation. Focal predictor: prop_manip = net_rearing_manipulation / rear_nest_CS, i.e. the signed fraction of the original clutch added (positive, enlarged broods) or removed (negative, reduced broods); larger values mean MORE sibling competition. Sample restricted to experimentally manipulated rearing broods (rear_nest_trt in {5=enlarged, 6=reduced}); the unmatched unmanipulated broods (trt 7) were excluded. Adjustment variables: Date_of_day14 (day-of-year of measurement) and year fixed effects (2001-2003) — lay date and clutch size were omitted as adjustment covariates because matched-pair assignment of the manipulation balances them by design; sensitivity model adjusting for them instead gave a nearly identical focal estimate (-1.90, SE 0.16). Estimate: -1.8543 g per unit proportional manipulation (SE 0.1606; z = -11.54, p < 0.001; mixed-model z inference, no small-sample df correction). Equivalently, a quarter-brood (25% of clutch) enlargement lowers day-14 mass by 0.464 g (SE 0.040), about 0.5 within-brood residual SD. Nest random-intercept variance 0.611, residual variance 0.575. Missing values were minimal: 52 chicks had missing rear_nest_LD (unused in final model); mass/tarsus complete. Conclusion: increased sibling competition significantly reduces nestling growth.
rows.predictor: Proportional brood-size manipulation, prop_manip = net_rearing_manipulation / rear_nest_CS (signed fraction of original clutch added to [enlarged] or removed from [reduced] the rearing brood), centered at 0; effect reported per +1.0 unit (100% of clutch added)

rows.note: Focal analysis: linear mixed-effects model (statsmodels MixedLM, ML) of day-14 nestling mass (g) on the signed net rearing-brood manipulation, fitted to the 2,716 chicks from the 319 experimentally manipulated rearing broods (trt 5 enlarged, net +1 to +4; trt 6 reduced, net -1 to -4). Unmanipulated broods (trt 7, n=919 chicks) were excluded because they were not matched to manipulated broods on clutch size or laying date. Adjustment: year fixed effects only (2001-2003); no nest-level date/clutch covariates, which is defensible because the matched-pair cross-fostering design balances laying date and clutch size across the manipulation by construction. Random intercept for rearing nest (chicks clustered within broods; nest variance 0.61 g^2, residual 0.58 g^2). Focal estimate: -0.180 g of day-14 mass per additional sibling chick added to the brood (95% CI -0.210 to -0.149; Wald z = -11.56, p = 6.4e-31; df_resid = 2,712; fitted n = 2,716 chicks / 319 broods; observation unit = chick; design = between-brood brood-size manipulation with chick-level clustering). Result robust to adjustment set: including rearing-nest hatch date and original clutch size gives -0.181 (SE 0.015) in the same 318-brood sample. Effect direction: more siblings (more competition) reduces nestling growth, consistent with the declared estimand.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation: signed net number of chicks added to the rearing brood at cross-fostering (positive = enlargement, negative = reduction); coefficient is change in day-14 mass (g) per additional sibling chick in the rearing brood

rows.note: Linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, REML) of day-14 tarsus length (mm) on the number of siblings/competitors in the rearing nest. Sample: ALL 3,720 chicks alive and measured at day 14, from all 452 rearing broods (167 enlarged, 165 reduced, 120 unmanipulated); no exclusions (outcome, brood size, hatch date, and nest ID are complete; '.'-coded strings coerced to numeric/NaN). Focal predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size, the realized number of chicks in the chick's rearing nest at day 14 (the actual competitor pool; larger = more sibling competition, so orientation as_declared, effect signed for that quantity). Adjustment covariates: rearing-nest hatching date (rear_nest_OH, linear) and breeding-season fixed effects (hatch_year 2001/2002/2003). Random intercept for rearing nest (chicks clustered within broods; mean 8.2 chicks/brood). Model converged; between-brood variance 0.158, residual variance 0.297. Focal result: −0.0236 mm tarsus per additional day-14 broodmate, SE 0.0069, z = −3.424, p = 6.2e-04 (z, model-based SE; mixed models use asymptotic normal inference, so z-statistic; df not applicable, denoted n=3,720 chick observations in 452 rearing broods). Sensitivity contrasts on other permissible scales gave consistent negative effects: per net sibling added (manipulated broods) tarsus −0.066 mm (z=−8.9) and mass −0.180 g (z=−11.6); per day-14 broodmate among manipulated broods −0.034 mm (z=−4.5). Interpretation: sibling competition significantly constrains nestling structural growth in this blue-tit population.
rows.predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size (number of chicks in the rearing nest at day 14; effect on day-14 tarsus length in mm per additional broodmate)

rows.note: Focal analysis: linear mixed model (ML) of day-14 nestling mass (g) in blue tits, fit to the 1,363 cross-fostered chicks (home_or_away==2, i.e., chicks experimentally moved into matched non-natal rearing broods) across 323 rearing nests; broods from all three treatment categories were represented via the realized rearing-brood size. Model: day_14_weight ~ d14_rear_nest_brood_size + rear_nest_LD + year (fixed effects) + random intercept for rearing nest (rear_nest_breed_ID). Focal predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size, the realized number of siblings/competitors in the rearing brood on day 14, entered linearly (grams per additional sibling); larger values = more siblings = more competition, so orientation is as_declared (negative sign = competition reduces growth). Estimate -0.1048 g per additional sibling (SE 0.0183, z = -5.71, p ~ 1e-8, residual df 1358; Wald z given between-nest df ~ 322, conclusion unchanged either way). Observations are chicks (unit), clustered in rearing nests (design: mixed model, chick-level residuals within nest-level random intercepts; nest random variance 0.88 g^2, residual 0.43 g^2). Exclusions: chicks not cross-fostered (retained home chicks), and rows with missing lay date or outcome. Sensitivity: alternative specifications (net experimental manipulation dose on manipulated broods, -0.18 g/sibling; realized brood size on manipulated broods, -0.11 g/sibling; covariate sets with clutch size/hatch date) all gave consistent negative effects, so the qualitative conclusion — each additional sibling reduces day-14 mass by roughly 0.1-0.2 g — is robust.
rows.predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size (realized number of siblings in the rearing brood on day 14, per additional sibling)

rows.note: Mixed-effects linear model (statsmodels MixedLM, REML), fitted to 2,716 chicks (day-14 survivors) in 319 experimentally manipulated rearing broods (trt 5 = enlarged, net manipulation +1 to +4; trt 6 = reduced, -1 to -4); the 919 chicks from 120 unmanipulated broods (trt 7) were excluded because unmanipulated nests were not matched to manipulated ones in clutch size or laying date. Outcome: PC1 of standardized day-14 mass and tarsus length (equal loadings 0.707/0.707; 80% variance explained) — a dimensionless overall nestling body-size index in SD units (raw mass and tarsus outcomes were disallowed by the analysis policy; both gave consistent negative effects of -0.180 g and -0.066 mm per sibling in sensitivity fits). Focal predictor: net_rearing_manipulation, signed count of chicks added (positive) or removed (negative) by the cross-fostering brood-size manipulation at ~1-2 days post-hatch. Covariates: rearing-nest hatching date (rear_nest_OH) and year fixed effects (2001-2003); chick sex omitted because missing for 1,094 chicks. Random intercept for rearing nest (accounts for clustering: mean 8.5 chicks/brood; between-brood var 0.52, residual var 0.83). Test statistic: z = -11.647, p = 2.4e-31 (MixedLM model-based SE; inferential df not defined for ML variance components — the design has 2,716 chick-level observations clustered in 319 nests). Interpretation: each additional sibling competitor reduces day-14 body size by ~0.17 SD, indicating a strong negative effect of sibling competition on nestling growth. Orientation as_declared: larger values of net_rearing_manipulation mean MORE siblings/competition.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (signed net chicks added to the rearing brood by the experimental cross-fostering manipulation; positive = enlarged brood = more sibling competition)

rows.note: Linear mixed model (REML, statsmodels MixedLM): day_14_tarsus_length (mm) ~ prop_manip + rear_nest_CS + rear_nest_LD + C(hatch_year), with a random intercept for rearing nest (rear_nest_breed_ID). Focal predictor prop_manip = net_rearing_manipulation / rear_nest_CS, i.e. the signed proportion of the rearing nest's original clutch experimentally added (positive) or removed (negative); fitted on experimentally manipulated broods only (rear_nest_trt in {5=enlarged, 6=reduced}; the unmatched unmanipulated broods, trt=7, excluded). Sample: 2,698 chicks from 317 rearing nests (observation unit = chick; chicks clustered within rearing broods, mean 8.5/brood). Estimate = -0.670 mm per unit proportional manipulation (z = -8.64, p < 0.001; model-based SE; mixed models use z inference, so inferential df is not finite/normal z-based). Equivalent per a 0.25 (quarter-clutch) enlargement: -0.168 mm (SE 0.019). Nest random-intercept variance 0.117; residual 0.313 mm^2. Larger prop_manip = more siblings = more competition, hence orientation as_declared. Exclusions: unmanipulated broods (design), missing lay date (52 chicks); sex excluded as covariate due to 29% missingness. Note the manipulation varied only between nests, so the nest random intercept is essential.
rows.predictor: proportional brood-size manipulation = net_rearing_manipulation / rear_nest_CS (signed fraction of the rearing nest's original clutch experimentally added or removed)

rows.note: Focal analysis: chick-level linear model, day_14_weight (g) ~ net_rearing_manipulation + Date_of_day14 + year fixed effects, with cluster-robust (sandwich) standard errors clustered on rearing nest (use_correction=True). Sample: manipulated broods only (rear_nest_trt 5=167 enlarged, 6=152 reduced; unmanipulated trt 7 dropped because not matched on clutch size or lay date): n=2,716 chicks from 319 rearing broods, 2001-2003 Wytham Wood blue tits. '.' codes coerced to NaN before analysis; weight/tarsus/manipulation complete, so no other exclusions; chick sex excluded as covariate due to 29% missingness. Test statistic: t = -11.513, cluster-robust df ≈ 314, p ≈ 1e-30. Observation unit: individual chick; design: matched-pair cross-fostering brood-size manipulation (net ±1 to ±4 chicks), nest-level assignment. Robustness: brood-level aggregation (n=319 nests, mean mass ~ net manipulation + year) gives -0.182 g/sibling (SE 0.016, t=-11.61, df=315); a nest random-intercept mixed model with hatch-date adjustment gives -0.180 (SE 0.016). All error structures agree. Interpretation: each additional sibling reduces day-14 mass by ~0.17 g (~1.6% of mean mass), indicating sibling competition substantially limits nestling growth.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation: signed net number of chicks added to (positive) or removed from (negative) the chick's rearing brood by the experimental cross-fostering manipulation, ranging -4 to +4; continuous per-sibling competition contrast

rows.note: Focal model: linear mixed model (REML, statsmodels MixedLM) of day-14 tarsus length (mm) on a signed treatment contrast "trt_contrast" = +1 for experimentally enlarged rearing broods (rear_nest_trt==5, net_rearing_manipulation +1..+4), -1 for experimentally reduced rearing broods (rear_nest_trt==6, net manipulation -1..-4). Sample: the 1,375 chicks alive and measured at day 14 that were themselves cross-fostered (home_or_away==2, reared away from the natal nest) within the enlarged/reduced rearing broods; restricting to moved chicks balances the being-moved experience across the enlarged-vs-reduced contrast. Unmanipulated broods excluded. Covariates: rearing-nest hatching date (rear_nest_OH, days) and breeding-season fixed effects (C(hatch_year), 2001-2003); random intercept for rearing nest (rear_nest_breed_ID). Nests decoded via cross-tab of rear_nest_trt with net_rearing_manipulation. Outcome and exposure complete in data; covariates '.'-coded values coerced to NaN; all 1,375 focal rows had complete tarsus, OH, nest ID. Result: estimate -0.1785 mm (half the enlarged-minus-reduced difference, i.e. enlarged broods ~0.36 mm shorter tarsus), SE 0.0266, z = -6.718, p = 1.8e-11; between-brood variance 0.160, residual 0.252; 325 rearing broods, mean 4.2 chicks/brood; observation unit = individual chick. Robustness: alternative operationalizations all gave negative effects (mass per net sibling -0.180 g, SE 0.016; tarsus per net sibling -0.066 mm, SE 0.007; tarsus per day-14 rearing-brood mate -0.034 mm, SE 0.008; full manipulated-sample contrast -0.190 mm, SE 0.023). Conclusion: sibling competition significantly reduces nestling structural growth. Test statistic: z (Wald). Inferential df: large-sample z (no finite df; 325 clusters, 1371 residual df contextually). Fitted n = 1375 chicks in 325 broods. Design: matched-pair brood-size cross-fostering manipulation, enlarged vs reduced rearing treatment; focal contrast is between-rearing-brood assignment, chick-level observations with nest random intercept.
rows.predictor: Signed rearing-treatment contrast: enlarged brood = +1 vs reduced brood = -1 (experimentally assigned sibling-competition level; coefficient = half the enlarged-minus-reduced difference in day-14 tarsus, mm)

rows.note: Focal model: chick-level OLS, day-14 body-size index (PC1 of standardized day-14 mass and tarsus; loadings -0.707/-0.707, ~80% joint variance, oriented so higher = larger) ~ net_rearing_manipulation + rear_nest_LD + year fixed effects, with rearing-nest cluster-robust (sandwich) standard errors (317 clusters). Sample: 2,698 chicks from 317 experimentally manipulated rearing broods (trt 5 enlarged / 6 reduced) in 2001-2003; unmanipulated broods (trt 7) excluded because they were not matched on clutch size or laying date; complete cases on outcome, manipulation, laying date, nest ID. Focal test: z = -11.152, p = 7e-29; residual df 2693; observation unit = individual chick at day 14; between-nest brood-manipulation design with cross-fostering. Robustness: mixed model (rearing-nest random intercept, hatch-date + year adjustment) on day-14 mass in grams gives -0.1799 g per extra sibling (SE 0.0155, z = -11.60), and the same LMM on the PC1 outcome gives -0.1728 (SE 0.0148), so the competition effect is stable across outcome and clustering choices. Interpretation: each extra sibling added to the rearing brood reduces nestling body size at day 14 by ~0.16 SD (roughly 0.18 g).
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (signed net chicks added to the rearing brood via experimental cross-fostering; range -4 to +4)

rows.note: Linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, REML) of day-14 nestling mass (g) on sibling competition, fit to the blue-tit cross-fostering dataset. Focal predictor: rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing — the number of nest-mates in the rearing brood immediately after the brood-size manipulation (the experimentally set competitive environment); larger values = more siblings = more competition, so orientation is as_declared and the estimate is signed for that quantity (negative = competition reduces growth). Covariates: rearing-nest hatching date (rear_nest_OH, centered implicitly) and breeding-year fixed effects (2001 baseline); random intercept for rearing nest (rear_nest_breed_ID). Outcomes and exposure complete; rows with missing rear_nest_OH dropped, giving n=3,333 chicks from 399 rearing broods (observation unit = chick; clustering by brood handled via the random intercept). Focal estimate -0.1528 g per additional sibling, SE 0.0124, t = -12.30, p ≈ 8.7e-35 (z-based inference; model df: 3 fixed-effect params + intercept + nest variance; residual variance 0.539, between-brood variance 0.595). Nuisance structure coherent: later hatch date (-0.051 g/day) and years 2002/2003 (-0.79/-0.86 g) associated with lighter chicks. Sensitivity context: an alternative manipulation-contrast model (net chicks added, manipulated broods only) gave -0.180 g/sibling (SE 0.016), and a day-14 brood-size model gave -0.084 g/sibling (SE 0.014) — all same direction and significance.
rows.predictor: rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing (number of siblings in the rearing brood at the start of rearing, i.e. post-manipulation nest-mate count), continuous, centered implicitly by model intercept; estimate is grams of day-14 mass per one additional sibling

rows.note: Linear mixed model (REML, statsmodels MixedLM): day_14_tarsus_length ~ d14_rear_nest_brood_size + rear_nest_CS_imp + rear_nest_LD_imp + C(hatch_year) + C(sex_f), random intercept for rearing nest (rear_nest_breed_ID). Outcome is day-14 tarsus length (mm), the structural size measure of nestling growth. Focal predictor is the realized rearing-nest brood size at day 14 (number of nestmates), a continuous signed count of the sibling-competition exposure; larger values = more competition (as_declared). Missing-data policy: full sample retained (n=3720 chicks, 452 rearing broods, no exclusions); chick sex (missing for 1094) entered as three-level factor male/female/unknown; missing lay dates (52) and clutch sizes (41) imputed with year-specific medians. Focal estimate = -0.0237 mm per additional nestmate (SE 0.0075, z = -3.140, 95% CI -0.038 to -0.009): each extra sibling reduces day-14 tarsus length by ~0.02 mm, a measurable cost of sibling competition. Among-nest variance 0.155 mm^2, within-nest residual 0.260 mm^2. Nest-level inferential df approx 452 - 8 = 444. Result matches the complete-case sensitivity fit (-0.026, SE 0.008), confirming robustness to the missing-data policy.
rows.predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size (realized number of nestmates in the rearing brood at day 14; larger = more sibling competition)

rows.note: Focal model: linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, REML) of day-14 nestling mass (g) on the realized day-14 rearing brood size (d14_rear_nest_brood_size, number of siblings present in the rearing nest at day 14), with rearing-nest hatch date (rear_nest_OH) and year fixed effects (2001 as reference) as covariates, and a random intercept for rearing nest (rear_nest_breed_ID). Analysis population: chicks from experimentally manipulated rearing broods only (rear_nest_trt 5 = enlarged [net manipulation +1 to +4, 1,742 chicks] and 6 = reduced [net manipulation -1 to -4, 1,059 chicks]); the unmatched unmanipulated broods were excluded. Fitted n = 2,801 chicks in 332 rearing broods (observation unit: chick; clustering by rearing nest, mean 8.4 chicks/nest). "." codings coerced to NaN; no focal-variable missingness in this subset. Focal estimate = coefficient of d14_rear_nest_brood_size = -0.1043 g per additional sibling (SE 0.0165, t/z = -6.32, p ~ 3e-10; model-based inference, z-statistic, so df is large-sample/asymptotic). Nest-level variance 0.81, residual variance 0.58. Larger brood size = more sibling competition = as_declared orientation (larger values mean MORE competition); the negative sign indicates more siblings reduce nestling growth, consistent across defensible alternative specifications (manipulation-count contrast: -0.180 g/chick, SE 0.016; all-chick brood-size gradient: -0.084 g/sibling, SE 0.014).
rows.predictor: Realized rearing brood size at day 14 (d14_rear_nest_brood_size): number of siblings/competitors actually present in a chick's rearing nest on the day of measurement; continuous, one signed coefficient per additional sibling.

rows.note: Focal analysis: linear mixed model (REML, statsmodels MixedLM) of day-14 tarsus length (mm) on a 0/1 dummy for experimentally enlarged rearing broods (rear_nest_trt=5, dummy=1) versus unmanipulated rearing broods (rear_nest_trt=7, dummy=0), with rearing-nest hatching date (rear_nest_OH) and breeding-year fixed effects (2001–2003) as covariates, and a random intercept for rearing nest (rear_nest_breed_ID). Sample: 2,661 chicks (1,742 enlarged, 919 unmanipulated) from 287 rearing broods (Wytham Wood blue tits, 2001–2003); chick-level observation unit, clustered by rearing nest (mean 9.3 chicks/brood). Exclusions: experimentally reduced broods (trt=6) excluded to keep a single focal contrast; rows missing tarsus, treatment, hatch date, or nest ID dropped (none for tarsus/treatment). Caveat: unmanipulated broods were not systematically matched to manipulated ones on clutch size or laying date, so the enlarged-vs-unmanipulated comparison is adjusted only by hatch date and year; the experimental enlarged-vs-reduced contrast (fitted as sensitivity, −0.381 mm, SE 0.045, z=−8.47) and continuous competition scales (tarsus per net sibling −0.066 mm, SE 0.007; tarsus per day-14 brood-mate −0.034 mm, SE 0.008; day-14 mass per net sibling −0.180 g, SE 0.016) all agree in direction and significance. Focal result: enlarged minus unmanipulated day-14 tarsus difference = −0.285 mm (95% CI −0.396 to −0.174), z = −5.016, p = 5.3e-07; between-nest variance 0.168, residual variance 0.316. Larger dummy values (enlarged = more siblings = more competition) correspond to MORE of the declared estimand, so the negative sign indicates that experimentally increased sibling competition reduces nestling growth. Native scale: mm difference in day-14 tarsus length; no conversion applied.
rows.predictor: 0/1 dummy for experimentally enlarged rearing brood (rear_nest_trt=5) vs unmanipulated rearing brood (rear_nest_trt=7); estimate is the adjusted day-14 tarsus length difference, enlarged minus unmanipulated, in mm

rows.note: Model: REML linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM), day-14 body-size index (PC1 of z-standardized day-14 mass and day-14 tarsus, equal loadings 0.707/0.707, 79.8% of joint variance, sign-oriented so larger = larger chick, native scale = SD units) ~ d14_rear_nest_brood_size + rear_nest_CS + rear_nest_LD + C(hatch_year), with a random intercept for rearing nest. Sample: 3,668 chicks from 446 rearing broods; 52 chicks dropped only for missing rearing-nest lay date; chick sex excluded because missing for ~30% of chicks (selection-bias risk). Brood size (the realized day-14 number of nestmates) is a nest-level predictor, so nest-level clustering is handled by the random intercept (among-nest variance 0.745, within-nest residual 0.795 SD^2). Focal result: each additional nestmate reduces day-14 body size by 0.0748 SD (SE 0.0160, z = -4.667, 95% CI -0.106 to -0.043). Test statistic: z (mixed-model Wald), inferential df approximately 440 (nests minus fixed effects, between-nest predictor). Observation unit: individual chick; design: chick-level cross-sectional day-14 measurements clustered in 452 rearing broods across enlarged (trt 5, net +1..+4), reduced (trt 6, net -4..-1), and unmanipulated (trt 7) treatments, Wytham Wood blue tits 2001-2003. Outcome is a general body-size composite because the experiment's growth effect is expected in both mass and structural size (separate component models gave concordant negative effects: mass -0.081 g/nestmate, tarsus -0.026 mm/nestmate).
rows.predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size: realized rearing-brood size at day 14 (continuous count of nestmates, per-chick focal contrast); larger values = more siblings/competition

rows.note: Linear mixed model (REML, statsmodels MixedLM): day_14_tarsus_length (mm, native linear scale) ~ prop_manip + rear_nest_CS + rear_nest_LD + C(hatch_year), with a random intercept for rearing nest (rear_nest_breed_ID). Focal predictor prop_manip = net_rearing_manipulation / rear_nest_CS, i.e. the signed fraction of the original clutch added (positive, enlarged broods, trt 5) or removed (negative, reduced broods, trt 6), zero for unmanipulated broods (trt 7). Sample: all complete-case chicks, n = 3,583 chicks in 433 rearing nests (all three treatment categories; 137 chicks excluded for missing rear_nest_LD). Observation unit: chick; clustering: chicks within rearing nests (mean 8.3 chicks/nest; nest-level variance 0.133 mm^2, within-nest residual 0.295 mm^2). Test statistic: z = -8.32 (Wald); MixedLM uses normal-approximation inference (no finite df; effective information at nest level, 433 nests). Estimate -0.671 mm per unit proportional manipulation means a quarter-of-clutch enlargement (the typical experimental magnitude) reduces day-14 tarsus length by ~0.17 mm (SE 0.02), ~30% of within-brood residual sd (0.54 mm). Robustness: the manipulated-broods-only version gives -0.670 (SE 0.078); a parallel model of day-14 mass gives -1.90 g per unit (SE 0.16). Interpretation: experimentally increased sibling competition significantly slows nestling structural growth.
rows.predictor: prop_manip = net_rearing_manipulation / rear_nest_CS (signed fraction of the original clutch added to or removed from the rearing brood; 0 for unmanipulated broods)

rows.note: Focal model: linear mixed model (ML, statsmodels MixedLM) of day-14 chick mass (g) on the realized number of competitors in the rearing nest at day 14 (d14_rear_nest_brood_size), adjusted for rearing-nest hatch date (rear_nest_OH) and original rearing-nest clutch size (rear_nest_CS), with a random intercept for rearing nest (rear_nest_breed_ID). Data: all 3,720 chicks with complete mass/tarsus; 41 rows dropped for missing hatch-date/clutch-size covariates, leaving n = 3,679 chicks from 447 rearing broods (observation unit: chick). Focal estimate: -0.0726 g per additional nest-mate (SE 0.0163, Wald z = -4.45, p ~ 1e-05; MixedLM uses large-sample z, no small-sample df). Nest random-intercept variance 0.83 g^2, residual 0.54 g^2. Signed quantity: the slope of d14_rear_nest_brood_size as entered (raw count); larger brood = more siblings = more competition, so negative sign means competition reduces growth. Sensitivity: an alternative model using the experimentally assigned net_rearing_manipulation among manipulated broods only (n=2,709 chicks, 318 broods; same covariates plus this design) gave -0.181 g per added chick (SE 0.015, z=-11.76), consistent in sign and magnitude per competition unit. Chick sex omitted (missing for 29% of chicks); year fixed effects omitted to keep the covariate set distinct from the pre-specified alternatives.
rows.predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size (number of nest-mates/competitors in the rearing brood at day 14, raw count)

rows.note: Focal model: OLS of day-14 nestling mass (g) on the signed net rearing brood manipulation (chicks added; +1 to +4 enlarged, -1 to -4 reduced), restricted to the 319 experimentally manipulated rearing broods (n = 2,716 chicks; 319 enlarged/reduced broods from the 452 in the file; unmanipulated broods excluded because they were not matched on clutch size or laying date). Adjusted for day-14 measurement date (Date_of_day14) and year fixed effects (2001-2003). Clustering handled with cluster-robust (sandwich) standard errors at the rearing-brood level (452->319 clusters; df ~ 314). Focal estimate: -0.1672 g of day-14 mass per sibling experimentally added to the rearing brood (SE 0.0145, t = -11.51, p ~ 1e-30). Robustness: two-way Cameron-Gelbach-Miller clustering on rearing nest AND hatch (natal) nest gives SE 0.0142 (t = -11.80, ~358 df), essentially unchanged; a rearing-nest random-intercept mixed model with a different adjustment set (hatch date + year) gave -0.180 g/sibling (SE 0.016) — same substantive conclusion. Observation unit: individual chick (clustered within rearing brood). Design: matched-pair brood-size manipulation via cross-fostering; larger values of the predictor = more siblings = more competition (as_declared). Conclusion: each additional sibling reduces day-14 nestling mass by ~0.17 g (~1.6% of mean mass), strong evidence that sibling competition limits nestling growth.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation: signed number of chicks experimentally added to the rearing brood via cross-fostering (positive = brood enlarged, negative = reduced), among manipulated broods only

rows.note: Focal model: chick-level OLS, day_14_weight (g) ~ net_rearing_manipulation + Date_of_day14 + year fixed effects, with cluster-robust (sandwich) SEs clustered on rearing nest (use_correction=True). Sample: ALL rearing broods (167 enlarged, 165 reduced, 120 unmanipulated), Wytham Wood blue tits 2001-2003; n=3,635 chicks in 439 broods (85 chicks dropped for missing Date_of_day14; weight complete). Focal predictor: net_rearing_manipulation, signed net chicks added (+, up to +4) or removed (−, to −4) by cross-fostering, 0 for unmanipulated; larger = more siblings = more competition (as_declared). Test: t = −11.537, ~434 cluster df, p ≈ 8.6e-31. Each additional sibling reduces day-14 mass by ~0.176 g (~1.7% of mean mass).
